literal: With eyes having sulked indeed, she became troubled; embracing, even more than me, she herself eagerness having felt.
translation: She feigned a sulk with her eyes, but quickly became distressed; feeling an eagerness to embrace even greater than mine, she hurried to me.
modern: அவள் தன் கண்களால் மட்டுமே ஊடல் கொண்டு சினந்தாள்; ஆனால் உடனே கலக்கமடைந்து, என்னை விடவும் அதிகமாகத் தழுவிக்கொள்ளும் விருப்பம் கொண்டு விரைந்தாள்.
explanation: This couplet captures a fleeting moment of a lovers' quarrel where the woman attempts to feign anger ('tuṉittē'). However, her anger is entirely superficial, restricted only to her eyes ('kaṇṇiṉ'), and she quickly becomes distressed ('kalaṅkiṉāḷ') at the thought of maintaining the distance. Overcome by an eagerness ('vituppu') for reunion that surpasses even the speaker's own desire ('eṉṉiṉum'), she abandons her pretense and hurries to embrace him. The contrast between her brief, visual sulk and her deep, urgent desire highlights the overpowering nature of their affection.
